chunks.h: Information for Diabetes Chairperson
chunks.t: Diabetes Chairpersons serve at the district and multiple district levels and are appointed by the district governor or council chairperson, respectively. Diabetes Chairpersons support Lions and Leos engaged or interested in projects to reduce the prevalence of diabetes and improve the quality of life for those diagnosed. They may collaborate with leadership throughout the organization, including the Global Service Team (GST). Learn Become the topic expert for your district/multiple district by learning about diabetes. Explore Goal 3 of the Sustainable Development Goals, which challenges the world to ensure healthy lives and promote well-being for all ages. Become familiar with the various types of diabetes: Type I, Type 2 and Gestational Diabetes. Learn more about obesity and its effects on overall health.

chunks.h: Information for Diabetes Chairperson
chunks.t: Explore Lion Portal, LCI/LCIF’s social media sites, and the annual Leo Video Contest to learn more about how Lions and Leos are addressing similar challenges in their communities. Discover Bring your knowledge to the local level by exploring how diabetes and its related conditions are directly impacting your district/multiple district. Conduct a Community Needs Assessment with a special focus on diabetes. Contact your national diabetes association, local department of public health, or similar organization, to learn about the needs in your area and which populations are at greatest risk of diabetes. Plan Based upon what you have learned and discovered, submit a plan of action, including recommended service goals for diabetes, to the district governor/council chairperson for approval.

chunks.h: Information for Diabetes Chairperson
chunks.t: In this process, you may wish to:Meet with organizations already working on diabetes to discuss how you might support, expand upon, or compliment their ongoing work. Collaborate with the Youth Camp and Exchange chairperson to organize a Youth Camp that includes youth with diabetes. Discuss your service plan with the GST Coordinator and other leaders, including other programmatic chairpersons, for their feedback. It is possible they are already implementing a project that would benefit from inclusion of a diabetes service element. Act Inspiring Lion and Leo clubs in your district/multiple district to serve and report their service to Lion Portal will be critical to the success of your plan. Become aware of Diabetes Resources.

chunks.h: Information for Diabetes Chairperson
chunks.t: Guide clubs in your district/multiple district through the “Learn, Discover, Act” journey as it pertains to diabetes. Build awareness of the need, the goals and the service plan by offering a diabetes-focused seminar and hands-on service activity during district/multiple district convention. Promote funding opportunities offered through LCI and LCIF that might support club/district diabetes projects. Formalize partnerships with other organizations to enhance local impact. Organize a district/multiple district donation to LCIF for diabetes and diabetic retinopathy to increase global impact. Establish and maintain open communication with the district governor, council chairperson and Global Service Team (GST) leaders. Celebrate Encourage clubs to thoroughly report their diabetes projects using the Lion Portal.

chunks.h: Information for Diabetes Chairperson
chunks.t: Keep the district governor/council chairperson and GST Coordinator informed. Discuss and evaluate progress of the action plan and goals. Share news about diabetes projects with the Public Relations Chairperson. Celebrate progress and success by recognizing all participating clubs. Contact Us Lions Clubs International Phone: 630-571-5466

16f19b3d8b.t: Second Vice District Governor Training Program

chunks.h: Second Vice District Governor Training Program
chunks.t: The Second Vice District Governor (SVDG) Training Program is designed to develop the leadership skills second vice district governors need to fulfill role-specific responsibilities and succeed as a member of the district governor team. The training blends self-paced, online courses in the Lions Learning Center, a live virtual seminar with fellow second vice district governors and local training coordinated by multiple/single district GLT coordinators or GAT area leaders. Please see the SVDG Program Overview and Frequently Asked Questions for more detailed information about the SVDG training program.

chunks.h: Second Vice District Governor Training Program
chunks.t: SVDG Program Overview Frequently Asked Questions Live virtual seminar SVDGs will be grouped with fellow SVDGs for a series of live virtual sessions which offer the opportunity to discuss topics such as LCIF, membership development and leadership development skills. The seminar will consist of six sessions beginning in November. Details regarding schedules and preparation materials will be communicated directly to SVDGs in August. The SVDG Virtual Seminar platform becomes available in October, with registration details being emailed directly to SVDGs. For assistance registering for the seminar and navigating the platform, view this help video.

chunks.h: Second Vice District Governor Training Program
chunks.t: View schedule VDG Multiple/Single District Workshop Lions International provides resources and curriculum for multiple districts and single districts to conduct a joint workshop for SVDGs and FVDGs in their area. This instructor-led workshop is organized by MD GLT coordinators in consultation with the GAT area leaders. Visit the Leadership Development Multiple District Grant Program webpage for more information. Online learning and assignments SVDGs will be assigned online courses to complete throughout their first year of training. The courses will be automatically assigned as they become available in the Lions Learning Center (LLC). Click the button below to access the Lions Learning Center and look for the SVDG Learning Path. Lions Learning Center Need help? Click here for access instructions.

chunks.h: Second Vice District Governor Training Program
chunks.t: For questions, please use the contact information below. SVDG Training Program +1 630-468-6857  Online Assignments Assistance +1 630-468-7073  Leadership Development Multiple District Grant Program and Training Curriculum +1 630-468-7172

chunks.h: The Leo-Lion Program
chunks.t: As a Leo-Lion, you have not only the ability to seamlessly continue your service journey, but also a variety of exclusive benefits that will help you grow even more as a Lion. Check out the opportunities that you have waiting for you. The benefits of Leo-Lion membership Being a Leo-Lion provides you with unique opportunities and benefits exclusive to your membership type. Explore the benefits you can take advantage of right now through your membership.

chunks.h: The Leo-Lion Program
chunks.t: Continued service with even more service opportunities Opportunity to mentor future Leos and share experience as a former Leo Networking opportunities with Lions of all ages to grow your knowledge of the organization Continued opportunities to grow as a leader Years of Leo service credited to your Lion record Option to serve in a Leo-Lion club or any other Lions club type Continued connection to the Leo identity under the name “Leo-Lion”50% discount on international dues*Entrance or charter fee waiver Exclusive Leo-Lion membership pin*You can choose to receive 50% off dues as a Leo-Lion whose membership does not count toward the club delegate count for international, multiple district, or district elections.

chunks.h: The Leo-Lion Program
chunks.t: You can also waive your dues discount in order to count towards your club's total delegate entitlement, provided you have been paying full dues for at least a year and a day. If you would like to waive your dues discount, please ask your club secretary or club president to make this change in the Lion Portal. In areas not using the Lion Portal, please contact your council chairperson and the general secretary. Tap into the Leo-Lion network You have the exclusive opportunity to join the Linked In Leo-Lion professional networking group, which can help you connect with fellow Leo-Lions around the world, share service and leadership ideas and much more. Join now Make the most of your membership There are many ways you can maximize your time as a Leo-Lion.

chunks.h: The Leo-Lion Program
chunks.t: From leadership opportunities like the Leo-Lion Board Liaison position to opportunities for personal growth and knowledge through our scholarship programs, every Leo-Lion journey is unique. Learn more about how you can make the most of your time as a Leo-Lion!Leadership positions Leo/Leo-Lion cabinet or council liaison - One-year, non-voting appointed roles aimed at fostering young leaders and strengthening Lions districts. Learn more about the resources available for Leo/Leo-Lion cabinet and council liaison roles. Leo-Lion Board Liaison - Serve as part of the Lions International Board of Directors. Meet your current Leo-Lion Board Liaisons!Scholarship opportunities Cultural Exchange Ambassador Scholarship - Awarded to Leo-Lion Cultural Exchange Ambassadors to represent your constitutional area, and attend forum sessions and events.

chunks.h: The Leo-Lion Program
chunks.t: Applications are currently closed. Read about the experience of former Cultural Exchange Ambassadors on the Lions Blog! Frequently asked questions What club options do I have as a Leo-Lion?Leo-Lion can join any kind of Lions club, and there are a variety of club types to choose from. Leo-Lions may be especially interested in chartering a Leo-Lion club, especially since they can be a great option for inviting their friends to join. Members aged 30 and younger joining a Leo-Lion club as a Young Adult member enjoy a 50% discount on international dues and a charter or entrance fee waiver like their Leo-Lion peers. Can Leo-Lions serve on committees, cabinets, councils and more?Yes! Lions International encourages multiple districts and districts to include Leo-Lions on their councils and cabinets.

chunks.h: The Leo-Lion Program
chunks.t: Leo-Lions have been representing young members at the international level since 2018, including the Leo-Lion board liaison position. I’m missing Leo years of service from my record. How can I credit them to my Lion member record?The first step is always to ensure accurate Leo club reporting and to ensure that your Leo membership was properly transferred when you became a Leo-Lion. Members can view their record on the Lion Portal to ensure accuracy. If you are an active Leo-Lion missing part of your Leo years of service, you may need to complete a Leo to Lion Certification form (LL-2). For members in the Leo-Lion program who need additional assistance, please reach out to  for assistance. I’m missing a Leo officer position from my record.

chunks.h: The Leo-Lion Program
chunks.t: How can I fix this?If you are missing a title from your Leo officer history on the Lion Portal, you can request to add the title(s) to your record by completing a Leo officer history update request (OH-101) form. I’ve heard that Leo-Lions can waive their international dues discount to count towards their club’s delegate entitlement. How can I waive my international dues discount?Leo-Lions have the option to waive their international dues discount to count towards their club’s total delegate entitlement, and additional information can be found in chapter XVII of Board Policy. Your Lions club secretary and president can waive your dues discount for you in the Lion Portal. For areas not using the Lion Portal, please contact your council chairperson and the general secretary.

chunks.h: The Leo-Lion Program
chunks.t: How do I get a Leo-Lion membership pin?All new active Leo-Lions will receive a free pin compliments of Lions Clubs International shipped directly to the member after they are added into the Lion Portal as a Leo-Lion member. Leo-Lions may purchase replacement pins from the Lions Shop. Delivery times vary, so allow reasonable time to receive your complimentary pin. Reach out to  for any assistance you may need. When should I expect to receive my Leo-Lion membership pin?A pin is shipped out directly to each member the month after they are added into the Lion Portal as a “Leo-Lion” member. Delivery times vary, so allow reasonable time to receive your complimentary pin. Reach out to  for any assistance you may need.

chunks.h: The Leo-Lion Program
chunks.t: Can anyone wear a Leo-Lion membership pin?The Leo-Lion pin is a membership program benefit exclusively for current active Leo-Lion members. The membership pin is not to be worn by those who are not Leo-Lions or those who are no longer eligible for the Leo-Lion program. Additionally, the Leo-Lion membership pin should not be gifted to non Leo-Lion members or used for trading. I’m interested in applying for the Leo-Lion scholarships. When are applications open?An application link will be available when applications open. They have historically opened in April–June but application opening times may vary each year. How can I serve as a Leo-Lion Board Liaison? Leo-Lion Board Liaisons are appointed by the International President annually.

chunks.h: The Leo-Lion Program
chunks.t: Each incoming international president determines their own method for identifying and appointing a Leo-Lion Board Liaison, so this process may change annually. Where can I find logos, social graphics, and guidelines for marketing as a Leo-Lion?Leo-Lions have an exclusive logo, social media kit and set of brand guidelines! Links to all of our social media kits, brand guidelines and additional information about effective marketing can be found on the Marketing Matters webpage. Expand the reach of Leo-Lions You have the opportunity and the influence to help guide Leos into their next steps as Leo-Lions. Learn how you can start a Leo-Lion club and encourage Leos to become Lions. Encourage Leos

chunks.h: Getting started with supporting Leos
chunks.t: Leos are devoted, innovative volunteers who realize the power of action. And as a Lion, you play a very important role in supporting their growth and development in a variety of ways so the Leos can thrive — and continue their service as Lions when the time is right. Get to know Leos Leos are some of the organization’s youngest — and most enthusiastic — volunteers. With their dedication and strong vision, Leos are helping to shape the future of our service. And together, Lions and Leos form a powerful partnership that strengthens our service and expands our impact.7,700+Leo clubs worldwide180,000+Leos150+countries and territories70,000+service projects each year Sponsor a club By sponsoring a Leo club, you’re in the best position to make Leos feel welcomed and help them succeed on their service journey.

chunks.h: Getting started with supporting Leos
chunks.t: And it’s not just beneficial for Leos — learn all the ways sponsoring a Leo club can positively impact your Lions club if you’re not already a sponsor. Success starts with your support There are so many great ways you can get involved and support Leos. Whether you enjoy working directly with Leos or prefer a more behind-the-scenes support role, you’ll find a position that’s right for you. Explore your options and see what role best suits you. Find your perfect role No matter how you want to support Leos, there’s a position for you. You can take a hands-on role as a Leo club advisor or take on a supportive role at the district or multiple district level. Or, if you’re interested in further growing the relationship between Lions and Leos internationally, you can apply to become a Leo Advisory Panel member.

chunks.h: Getting started with supporting Leos
chunks.t: Get involved Amplify your impact While there are specific positions for Lions who want to support Leos, any and every Lion should work with their Leos in planning, serving and celebrating. Because more hands means more service — and more fun along the way with your Leos!Learn more Encourage Leos to become Lions One of the best ways any Lion can support Leos is to let them know about their options to continue serving as Lions — especially as they near the end of their time in the Leo Club Program. Explore tips and resources designed to help you encourage Leos aging out of the program to transition to Lions. Get started

483e87a3a2.t: Leo District and Multiple District Leadership

chunks.h: Leo District and Multiple District Leadership
chunks.t: Promoting the Leo Club Program at the district and multiple district levels is an important part of ensuring Leos are supported in their service, membership and transition to becoming Lions. Photo by: Lion Othmar Fetz, The LEO Book On this page Leo district and multiple district officers and chairpersons can find helpful resources for running district and multiple district-level Leo events as well as an overview of leadership positions. Leo and Lion leaders can find an overview of the Leo district and multiple district structure in the Lions Board Policy, Chapter 22.

chunks.h: Leo District and Multiple District Leadership
chunks.t: Leo district/multiple district leader roles Hosting leadership trainings Applying for Leo grants for your district/multiple district Encouraging Leo club reporting in the Lion Portal Reporting a Leo district/multiple district Leo district and multiple district leadership roles Explore the list below to learn more about the roles and responsibilities of these Leo and Lion leadership positions. District and multiple district Leo chairpersons Leo chairpersons contribute to the success of their districts through the promotion, development and continued support of Leo clubs. District and multiple district chairpersons should promote reporting of Leos in their areas and ensure that Leo clubs and membership totals are accurate and that Leo participation in learning and development events is reported in the Learn digital tool.

chunks.h: Leo District and Multiple District Leadership
chunks.t: They can also assist with the appointment of Leos or Leo-Lions as cabinet and council liaisons. We encourage Leo chairpersons to coordinate efforts with GMT coordinators and Leo club advisors to celebrate Leos and identify opportunities for those in their last years of Leo service. This includes identifying clubs supportive of younger members and creating new clubs for Young Lions.

chunks.h: Leo District and Multiple District Leadership
chunks.t: District and multiple district Leo chairperson resources District Leo Chairperson Responsibilities and Appointment Form Multiple District Leo Chairperson Responsibilities and Appointment Form Young Lions Hub Leo to Lion Resources Positive Collaboration with Lions and Leos webpage Why Start a Leo Club presentation and video Leo or Leo-Lion cabinet and council liaison The Leo or Leo-Lion cabinet and council liaison positions are one-year, non-voting appointed positions developed to engage young leaders and strengthen Lions districts and multiple districts. This position is an opportunity to further a Leo or Leo-Lion's leadership skills, use their experience to improve the Leo Club Program and represent the diverse views of young people in their area.

chunks.h: Leo District and Multiple District Leadership
chunks.t: These liaisons can also support recording membership growth in their area by promoting the importance of Leo reporting to both Leos and Lions. Liaisons should also support the Leo to Lion transition by working with their respective chairperson and GMT coordinator to celebrate Leos and identify membership opportunities for those in their last years of Leo service. Leo cabinet and council liaison resources Role Description: Leo and Leo-Lion Cabinet and Council Liaisons Model District Cabinet Structure Leo-Lion Program webpage Leo to Lion Resources About Leos webpage Positive Collaboration with Lions and Leos webpage Leo district and multiple district presidents Leo district and multiple district presidents and vice presidents are elected annually.

chunks.h: Leo District and Multiple District Leadership
chunks.t: Upon election, the presidents can appoint the districts or multiple districts secretaries and treasurers if the Leo district and multiple district secretaries and treasurers were not elected. Leo district and multiple district officers provide leadership training seminars for Leos, promote unified service activities and/or fundraising campaigns and encourage active involvement in the Leo Club Program. Leo district and multiple district presidents can also help support membership growth in their areas by working with their district or multiple district Leo membership chairperson.

chunks.h: Leo District and Multiple District Leadership
chunks.t: Leo district and multiple district president resources Leo Club Advisory Panel Improving Your Leo Club: Checklist for Leos Leo Club Reporting Resources Leo district and multiple district membership chairpersons The Leo district/multiple membership chairperson is a Leo who plans and implements the recruitment strategy for the district/multiple district. This position should work with their district leadership to encourage membership reporting, develop area-wide strategies and share recruitment best practices with clubs in their district. The membership chairperson is an optional position, reporting to either the district/multiple district president or vice president. This role can be appointed or elected as determined by the constitution and bylaws of the district/multiple district.

chunks.h: Leo District and Multiple District Leadership
chunks.t: Leo district and multiple district membership chairperson resources Leo Recruitment video Just Ask! Quick reference guide Leo Pride webpage Leo recruitment brochure Leo social media templates Hosting leadership trainings The Leo Club Advisor Training & Orientation page is designed to provide Leo club advisors with a clearer understanding of the Leo Club Program and the role of an advisor. Districts and multiple districts can use this page to guide hosting a workshop series for Leo club advisors in their area and promote it as a valuable reference for Lions involved in the program. District and multiple district leaders should hold Leo club officer trainings and establish an annual Leo learning and development calendar.

chunks.h: Leo District and Multiple District Leadership
chunks.t: They should also encourage Leo members to grow their learning record by participating in locally planned Leo learning events (such as the Leo Advancement Sessions) and completing courses in the Lions Learning Center (LLC). Access the LLC in Learn using your Lion Portal login credentials or click here for Lion Portal access instructions. Reporting Leo Learning Events in the Learn App Learn Leo Reporting Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) Leo Leadership Development Opportunities Applying for Leo grants Districts and multiple districts are eligible for two Leo specific grants. The Leo Leadership Grant Program provides up to US$2,000 in funding for events focused on developing Leos' leadership skills.

chunks.h: Leo District and Multiple District Leadership
chunks.t: The LCIF Leo Service Grant gives up to US$5,000 to Leos that are planning a service project and need additional funds to make a greater impact in their community. Visit the Leo Grants page to learn more. Encouraging Leo clubs to report in the Lion Portal District and multiple district officers should use the Lion Portal to ensure that their area's club and membership information is up to date. They should also encourage Leo club officers and Leo club advisors to report and manage their membership rosters and access new member resources in the Lion Portal. Ensure Leos in your region receive important messages from Lions International and encourage clubs to report officers and members.

chunks.h: Leo District and Multiple District Leadership
chunks.t: Reporting resources Why Reporting is Important Reporting a Leo district or multiple district To officially establish a Leo district or multiple district, the Leo club chairperson must report district/multiple district officers in the Lion Portal. If your district or multiple district does not use the Lion Portal, the Annual Report for Leo Districts and Multiple Districts (Leo-91) can be submitted each fiscal year. Lions districts with six or more Leo clubs may form a Leo district with the approval of the district governor. Lions multiple districts with 10 or more Leo clubs may form a Leo multiple district with the approval of the council of governors. Leo membership within the multiple district must exceed 100.

5479682836.t: Global Action Team (GAT) Roles and Resources

chunks.h: Global Action Team (GAT) Roles and Resources
chunks.t: As a member of the GAT, your success is our success. Whether you’re a part of the Global Membership Team (GMT), Global Extension Team (GET), Global Leadership Team (GLT), or Global Service Team (GST) you’ll find valuable information and resources on this page that will help you better understand your role and make a greater impact. You can also learn more about the GAT by taking the Global Action Team course available in the Lions Learning Center using your Lion Portal login credentials. A mission powered by the GAT. MISSION 1.5 is our drive to reach 1.5 million members worldwide on July 1, 2027. Leaders at every level are invested and responsible for success — so GAT leaders will be the example they can follow by encouraging collaboration and accountability at every level.

chunks.h: Global Action Team (GAT) Roles and Resources
chunks.t: The Global Action Team is uniquely positioned as the best resource to help you achieve MISSION 1.5 targets and foster membership growth. Learn more about your individual roles and responsibilities for MISSION 1.5 and as a GAT leader below. GAT priorities Membership growth, leadership development, and service are crucial to the success of any Leo or Lions club. To help clubs continue their growth, the GAT has prioritized the combined strategies of the Global Membership Approach, MISSION 1.5 and our district goals process. The Global Membership Approach equips districts with a strategic process focused on rejuvenating districts with new clubs, revitalizing clubs with new members and re-motivating existing members with fellowship and exciting service to help districts achieve their MISSION 1.5 targets.

chunks.h: Global Action Team (GAT) Roles and Resources
chunks.t: By aligning the approach with this global membership initiative, districts will develop their own unique opportunities and distinct paths to grow membership, strengthen clubs and increase service. This is done by developing district goals and action plans that are directly tailored to support membership development, leadership development, service activities and LCIF. Action plans to support MISSION 1.5 targets will be submitted through the District Goals process. Roles and responsibilities The GAT is made up of members from every level of Lions International. In the dropdowns below, you’ll find helpful links to overviews of the various positions within the GAT, which include, but are not limited to, the GMT, GET, GLT and GST.

63c024e496.t: Top Ten Youth Camps and Exchange Chairperson Award

chunks.h: Top Ten Youth Camps and Exchange Chairperson Award
chunks.t: The success of the Youth Camps and Exchange (YCE) Program can be attributed to the unwavering dedication of Lions around the world who serve as YCE chairpersons. The annual Top Ten Youth Camps and Exchange Chairperson Award recognizes and honors those Lions who go above and beyond their duties as YCE chairpersons. View the winners Award eligibility, criteria and achievement narrative All official district and multiple district YCE chairpersons are eligible for the Top Ten Youth Camps and Exchange Chairperson Award. Immediate past council chairpersons and immediate past district governors are encouraged to nominate an extraordinary YCE chairperson that served during the camp and exchange period in the previous fiscal year.

chunks.h: Top Ten Youth Camps and Exchange Chairperson Award
chunks.t: Some considerations for this award include:Being registered in Lion Portal as YCE Chairperson for the award year Being nominated by their Immediate Past Council Chairperson (District or Multiple District YCE Chairpersons) or Immediate Past District Governor (District YCE Chairpersons only) Nominations are weighed considering the following criteria and answers to prompts.

chunks.h: Top Ten Youth Camps and Exchange Chairperson Award
chunks.t: Criteria Number of outgoing and incoming youth participants Geographic diversity (number of regions/countries represented) Promotion of peace, international understanding and goodwill Inclusion of Lions service and global causes Program innovation and development Prioritization of positive participant experience, including youth safety Achievement narrative“Describe why you’re nominating this chairperson for the Top Ten Youth Camps & Exchange Chairperson Award.”“How did this chairperson integrate service into their YCE program?”“How did this chairperson effectively engage or integrate their community as part of their YCE program?”“Describe how this chairperson facilitated a cultural, educational, and innovative experience for all participants of their YCE program.”“Describe how this chairperson prioritized youth protection, safety, and a positive experience for all participants of their program.” Nominate your YCE chairperson If you know a YCE chairperson who meets the criteria for the award, consider nominating them using our easy-to-use form.

chunks.h: Top Ten Youth Camps and Exchange Chairperson Award
chunks.t: Nominations can be submitted from July 1 to August 15 each year.

chunks.h: Top Ten Youth Camps and Exchange Chairperson Award
chunks.t: Submit nomination 2024-2025 YCE top ten chairpersons The following individuals were selected by the Lions International Board of Directors Service Activities Committee for their service in positively impacting the lives of young people around the world and fulfilling the Lions Clubs International mission to encourage peace and international understanding through Lions clubs."A significant aspect of serving as YCE Chairperson is traversing the state of Michigan, visiting various districts and clubs, meeting new Lions members, and getting to know Lions from other countries and parents of our participants."Elvira Marfil Multiple District 11 (United States)"The YCE program enables young people to participate in social service abroad and learn about the global service of Lions Clubs, truly living out the spirit of 'We Serve.'"Tan-Hua Yang District 300B 6 (China, Taiwan)"One of the most memorable moments is seeing the impact on returning exchange participants as they share how the program broadens their cultural understanding and builds lifelong friendships."Amritveer Singh Sohal District 301 C (Philippines)"What I love most about the YCE program is when we Lions can say at the end of camp every year that twenty youngsters came as strangers and they are leaving as friends."Christian Rathmann District 111NH (Germany)"The YCE program is always memorable.

chunks.h: Top Ten Youth Camps and Exchange Chairperson Award
chunks.t: Bringing together young people from all over the world and giving them experiences that they will cherish for the rest of their lives is one of the things I am most passionate about. Building a spirit of understanding also comes through getting to know others who are so different yet so similar in their dreams, hopes, and interests."Paola Forneris District 108IA3 (Italy)"From exchange youth, visiting youth, host families and camp staff, I heard that although they were anxious at first, they felt deep bonds and the stimulation of different cultures.

chunks.h: Top Ten Youth Camps and Exchange Chairperson Award
chunks.t: They were truly glad they participated in the YCE program."Yuichi Nakata District 334 E (Japan)"Serving as YCE chairperson has been a truly rewarding journey, opening doors to global connections, meaningful learning, and unforgettable friendships while experiencing the powerful unity of youth across borders."Shalini Bhargava District 3233G2 (India)"The main purpose of the YCE program is to cultivate young leaders, which is very meaningful for society. It provides opportunities for young people from around the world to engage in global service.

chunks.h: Top Ten Youth Camps and Exchange Chairperson Award
chunks.t: This is a very important and unforgettable experience for the growth of young people."Yumi Pui Yu Leung District 303 (China)"What I love most about the YCE program is listening to the young people as they prepare and welcoming their concerns, emotions, curiosity, and excitement ... it's like hearing someone call you 'mom' for the first time."Sandra Becostrino District 108 L (Italy)“The greatest joy for me is to continue promoting the expansion of the program to families overseas and the opportunity to meet friends with whom we can maintain lifelong connections.”Hideo Dan Multiple District 335 (Japan)

chunks.h: Logos and Emblems
chunks.t: The Lions Clubs International emblem is recognized around the world as a symbol of kindness and service. Within our brand, there are several icons, logos and emblems that represent our various initiatives. We’ve created this page to provide the brand-approved versions for you to use. File Formats and Proper Usage JPG: Used for print and digital mediums (websites, presentation tools, collateral etc). Solid white background behind logo. PNG: Used for print and digital mediums (websites, presentation tools, collateral etc). Ideal for when you need a logo with a transparent background. EPS: Used for printed collateral produced by professional design programs (Adobe In Design, Illustrator etc). Can be scaled to any size without sacrificing quality. Often referred to as “vector” format.

chunks.h: Logos and Emblems
chunks.t: These are the only emblems that may reproduced electronically or otherwise, including sites on the World Wide Web and other areas on the Internet. Downloaded (or those procured electronically) official emblems may only be used according to the emblem use policy of Lions Clubs International. Generally, Lions clubs and districts have license to use the emblem on Web pages, stationery and other printed material. No Lion, Lions club or Lions district may use the association's emblem on any item sold to Lions or the general public for fundraising purposes. No manufacturer, printer, producer, promoter, publisher, entrepreneur may use the association's name, goodwill, trademarks, service marks or the Lions Clubs International emblem in any manner except upon license granted by the association.

chunks.h: Logos and Emblems
chunks.t: For information about securing a license, contact the association's General Counsel at (630) 571-5466, ext 299 or e-mail  or contact the Club Supplies and Distribution Division at (630) 571-5466, ext 252 or e-mail at .

a2b8e8cc4f.t: Leo and Leo-Lion Awards and Recognition

chunks.h: Leo and Leo-Lion Awards and Recognition
chunks.t: Lions International offers an array of awards to recognize Leos and Lions who are active in the Leo Club Program, as well as Leo-Lions. There are more than 20 award programs to acknowledge their accomplishments. Please note that only Leo and Lion officers reported to Lions International are eligible to receive awards and certificates. Processing time: Please allow 2-4 weeks after receipt of required forms. Leo Awards Individual Leos, Leo club advisors and Leo clubs as well as their sponsoring clubs have the opportunity to earn a variety of prestigious awards. Check out all the available awards and their qualifications.

chunks.h: Leo and Leo-Lion Awards and Recognition
chunks.t: Individual Leo and Leo Advisor Awards Leos of the Year Award: A multiple district council of governors or single district (that is not part of a multiple district) may nominate one high-achieving Leo each year for this medallion and certificate award. Applications must be submitted by March 1. Congratulations to all the current award recipients!Leo Club President Achievement Award: A Leo club president who meets specific requirements during their year in office may be awarded this certificate by the Leo club advisor with the approval of the sponsoring Lions club president. Award criteria categories include leadership development, membership extension, administration and Leo club activities. Certificate will be emailed to Leo club advisors in May.

chunks.h: Leo and Leo-Lion Awards and Recognition
chunks.t: Leo October Membership Growth Award: Leo club advisors may present this award to any Leo who is reported in the Lion Portal as a sponsor for at least three new members who join during the month of October. Leo club advisors whose Leos meet the above criteria by November 15 will be sent the award automatically; no application is necessary. Leo Award of Honor: Leos may nominate a fellow Leo member for this award to recognize their outstanding accomplishments during the year. The lapel medal can be purchased from the Lions Shop. Leo Club Advisor Outstanding Service Award: The Leo club president may present this award to Leo club advisors who meet specific requirements and demonstrate outstanding service in guiding and developing their Leo clubs. Nomination forms are accepted April-June each year.

chunks.h: Leo and Leo-Lion Awards and Recognition
chunks.t: Leo Club Advisor Five-Year Service Award: Sponsoring Lions club presidents may honor Leo club advisors who successfully complete five years of dedicated service with this award. Sponsoring Lions club presidents should complete and submit this application to obtain the five-year service pin and certificate. Leo Club Sponsorship Recognition Award: Sponsoring Lions club presidents and Leo club advisors receive these certificates upon official certification of a new Leo club. The sponsoring Lions club can request additional certificates by emailing  for anyone it wishes to thank for assisting in organizing the new Leo club. Leo Clubs and Sponsoring Lions Clubs Leo Club Pride Award: Leo clubs that have excelled in reporting their service, member and officer information will receive the Leo Club Pride Award.

chunks.h: Leo and Leo-Lion Awards and Recognition
chunks.t: Clubs who meet the following criteria based on reports in the Lion Portal by June 30 will be sent the award automatically; no application is necessary. Leo Club Excellence Award: All districts may endorse one Leo club to receive this prestigious award. Applications are due May 31. Winners will receive a banner patch and chevron in Leo colors. Congratulations to all the current award recipients!Serving Together Award: A banner patch featuring the Leo and Lions club logo is awarded to both the Leo club and the sponsoring Lions club for successful completion of joint projects and other types of activities supporting Leo and Lion collaboration. Award requirements are on the application. Award can be received once per Lion year. Ideas to successfully work together can be found on the Leo and Lion Positive Collaboration webpage.

chunks.h: Leo and Leo-Lion Awards and Recognition
chunks.t: Leo Club and Sponsoring Lions Club Anniversary Patches: Leo clubs who have achieved the fifth anniversary of their certification and their sponsoring Lions club can receive anniversary patches sent from the Leo Club Program staff. Patches are sent for anniversaries in multiples of five years thereafter. To receive the anniversary patch, please complete the following form. Leo Club Sponsorship Patch: A banner patch is issued to the sponsoring Lions club upon certification of a new Leo club. Leo District and Multiple Districts Leo District President Achievement Award: A Leo district president who meets specific requirements during their year in office may be awarded this certificate at the end of the Lion year by the district Leo chairperson with the approval of the district governor.

chunks.h: Leo and Leo-Lion Awards and Recognition
chunks.t: Award criteria categories include leadership development, club or membership extension, administration and district Leo activities. Certificate will be emailed to district Leo chairpersons in May. Leo Multiple District President Achievement Award: A Leo multiple district president who meets specific requirements during their year in office may be awarded this certificate at the end of the Lion year by the multiple district Leo chairperson with the approval of the council chairperson. Award criteria categories include leadership development, club or membership extension, administration and multiple district Leo activities. Certificate will be emailed to multiple district Leo chairpersons in May.

chunks.h: Leo and Leo-Lion Awards and Recognition
chunks.t: Leo Club Extension Award: Certificates are awarded to district Leo chairpersons and Leo district presidents who achieve a net gain of three new clubs in their district, and to multiple district Leo chairpersons and Leo multiple district presidents who achieve a net gain of five new clubs in their multiple district by June 30. Additional eligibility criteria includes that all new Leo clubs must report all members and their five club officers, and at least one service project must be reported in the Lion Portal during that fiscal year. No application is necessary. Leo-Lion Awards Leo-Lion awards are automatically processed after the end of each fiscal year — no need to apply!

chunks.h: Leo and Leo-Lion Awards and Recognition
chunks.t: Processing for these awards will occur after June 30 of each fiscal year so that data from the entire fiscal year can be used, and certificates will be sent in the following months. Leo-to-Lion Transition Awards Leo to Leo-Lion Membership Award: Special certificates are awarded to Leo club advisors, district Leo chairpersons and multiple district Leo chairpersons who have facilitated the transition of Leos to Leo-Lion members between July 1 through June 30. The following criteria applies for these awards: Leo club advisors: Guide five or more Leos from their Leo clubs to transition to Leo-Lion members. District Leo chairpersons: Facilitate Leo to Leo-Lion membership for 15 or more Leos from Leo clubs within their district.

chunks.h: Leo and Leo-Lion Awards and Recognition
chunks.t: Multiple district Leo chairpersons: Facilitate Leo to Leo-Lion membership for 30 or more Leos from any districts within their multiple district. Awards for Sponsoring Leo-Lion Clubs Leo-Lion Club Charter Award: Special certificates are awarded to sponsoring Lions clubs, district governors, district Leo chairpersons and multiple district Leo chairpersons who have facilitated the new charters of one or more Leo-Lion clubs. Completed charters must be approved by Lions Clubs International between July 1 through June 30 of the respective fiscal year. The following criteria applies for these awards: Lions clubs: Sponsor one or more newly chartered Leo-Lion clubs. District Leo chairpersons and district governors: Facilitate one or more new Leo-Lion club charters within their district.

chunks.h: Leo and Leo-Lion Awards and Recognition
chunks.t: Multiple district Leo chairpersons: Facilitate one or more new Leo-Lion club charters within any of their districts. Leo and Leo-Lion Awards Presidential Awards Initiatives Presidential awards are created annually and may include additional awards regarding Leos, Leo-Lions or the membership of young people. See this year’s presidential awards to find out more about whether awards are available regarding Leos and Leo-Lions. LCIF Awards Leos and Leo-Lions are eligible for a number of awards and recognition presented by the Lions Clubs International Foundation (LCIF). These include a certificate of appreciation, LCIF Chairperson’s certificate, Melvin Jones Fellowship, banner patch and club plaque award. Contact LCIF for more information.

chunks.h: Leo and Leo-Lion Awards and Recognition
chunks.t: Kindness Matters Service Award The Kindness Matters Service Award is a prestigious award that is given annually to a handful of Lions and Leo clubs for performing an outstanding service project in one of Lions International’s global cause areas. Nominated at the club level, the Kindness Matters Service Award is a challenge for Lions and Leos to develop exceptionally innovative and creative service projects with the aim of leaving a positive impact in their communities. Lions International Marketing Award Leo and Leo-Lion clubs have the chance to be recognized for great club marketing. Clubs must plan and execute a marketing campaign that meets the award criteria and only one Leo or Lion club per constitutional area will win. Check out the full award details and apply here.

chunks.h: Leo and Leo-Lion Awards and Recognition
chunks.t: If you have questions or need more information about any Leo or Leo-Lion awards, contact the Young Lions and Leos Department staff.

a8701cba38.t: Global Membership Team and Global Extension Team Toolbox

chunks.h: Global Membership Team and Global Extension Team Toolbox
chunks.t: Growing our membership is essential for realizing our vision of being the global leader in humanitarian and community service. New members inspire our clubs with new energy and ideas while providing the next generation of Lion leaders. New clubs extend our reach into new communities, allowing us to serve more people in new ways. The Global Membership Team (GMT) supports membership development by recruiting new members and promoting positive membership experiences. The Global Extension Team (GET) is an offshoot of the Global Membership Team that is focused on starting new clubs within its district. Want to get to know these roles more in depth? Check out the GMT coordinator and GET coordinator position descriptions and their respective annual checklists (GMT/GET).

chunks.h: Global Membership Team and Global Extension Team Toolbox
chunks.t: Take a look at the GET Coordinator Power Point to learn more about how the GET can help you reach your chartering goals. The resources below will guide you as you lead membership and club growth in your district. Global Membership Approach The Global Membership Approach is a four-step process that has been proven to increase both member satisfaction and new member recruitment, as well as new club chartering. The four steps are build a team, build a vision, build a plan and build success. Visit the Global Membership Approach webpage to learn more about how the Global Membership Approach can help your district develop and achieve its growth goals. As part of the build a vision step, you’ll need to visit the Membership Reports Toolbox to find the current status of membership in your district.

chunks.h: Global Membership Team and Global Extension Team Toolbox
chunks.t: It features reports on five-year growth trends, club and district health reports, and more. Zone and region chairpersons play important roles in achieving your membership growth goals. The Global Membership Approach for region and zone chairpersons webpage has resources to support them. Starting new clubs The start a new club webpage has everything you need to know about starting a club. We recommend starting with the New Club Development Guide. Consider making specialty clubs a part of your new club strategy. These clubs are organized around a common interest rather than geography. Recruiting new members Lion leaders have found the following resources to be helpful in bringing in new members.

chunks.h: Global Membership Team and Global Extension Team Toolbox
chunks.t: Always remember that everyone in your community is a potential Lion!Membership Development Grants: Districts and multiple districts can apply for funding to recruit new members and/or start new clubs. Just Ask: New Member Recruiting Guide for Clubs: This comprehensive guide uses the Global Membership Approach process to show you how to recruit new Lions. Use social media to grow your club’s visibility and membership. These blogs share practical tips to strengthen your presence, post with purpose and turn online engagement into new members. Strengthening your Social Presence Posting with a Purpose Turn Your Followers Into Members Lions clubs offer a unique opportunity for people of all ages to serve their community together.

chunks.h: Global Membership Team and Global Extension Team Toolbox
chunks.t: Sponsoring Leo clubs increases the service in your district, makes membership more appealing to families and builds the next generation of Lion leaders. Learn more about the Leo Club Program. Improving member experience People can serve their communities anywhere, but they become Lions for the fellowship. These resources will help keep your members engaged and show where you have areas to improve. Exceeding Expectations: This survey provides clubs the opportunity to gather the opinions of their members to improve member satisfaction. Member Satisfaction Guide: Strategies for how to keep Lions happy and active.

chunks.h: Global Membership Team and Global Extension Team Toolbox
chunks.t: Lions Network: Learn how to set up a network of like-minded Lions in your district Lions Learning Center Lion leaders have found the following online courses in the Lions Learning Center to be helpful in growing membership and starting new clubs:New Club Development course The Global Action Team course Conflict Resolution course Global Membership Approach Orientation Engaging Leos Global Action Team Global Leadership Team Toolbox Global Service Team Toolbox Lions Clubs International staff is here to help answer any questions you might have. You can email us at .

b20b7e9cf6.t: LCIF and World Food Program USA

chunks.h: LCIF and World Food Program USA
chunks.t: Nourishing futures through school meals Lions Clubs International Foundation (LCIF) and World Food Program USA partner to expand access to nutritious school meals through the United Nations World Food Programme home-grown school meals program. Together, we are helping children stay in school, strengthening local agriculture and creating opportunity in communities where hunger threatens a child’s future. A growing partnership against hunger Lions Clubs International Foundation (LCIF) and World Food Program USA launched a joint partnership in 2024 to support the United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) home-grown school meals initiative.

chunks.h: LCIF and World Food Program USA
chunks.t: Through a combined US$4 million investment, US$2 million from each organization, the partnership began supporting school meal programs that improve nutrition, increase school attendance and strengthen local food systems. Building on early success, the partnership expanded for three additional years with an annual commitment of US$2 million from LCIF and US$2 million from World Food Program USA. In 2026, programs support children and communities in Ghana, Honduras, Kenya, Madagascar, Nicaragua, Nepal and Uganda, with local Lions working alongside country offices and schools to strengthen community engagement and program support. In Karamoja, Uganda, a daily school meal can mean the difference between hunger and hope.

chunks.h: LCIF and World Food Program USA
chunks.t: Watch how LCIF and World Food Program USA help children stay in school while supporting local farmers and strengthening communities. Meaningful progress together The home-grown school meals model connects child nutrition, education and local agriculture to create sustainable solutions to hunger. Seven countries supported in 2026Ghana, Honduras, Kenya, Madagascar, Nicaragua, Nepal and Uganda. US$2 million committed annually by LCIFSupporting the United Nations World Food Programme home-grown school meals program over the next three years.653,000+ students reached Through the delivery of 1.8 million pounds of food over the first two years of the partnership. Just US$0.25 can provide a school meal, US$1 helps provide four school meals and US$50 can feed a child for a full year.

chunks.h: LCIF and World Food Program USA
chunks.t: Donate today LCIF and World Food Program USA in the news How Our Partnerships Fueled Progress Against Hunger in 2025January 29, 2026 – Ending hunger requires more than food. It takes innovation, logistics expertise and the shared commitment of people and organizations working together to create lasting change. Media clip in English only. Read more Sri Lanka’s National School Meal Programme Gets US$1 Million Donation April 23, 2025 – Sri Lanka’s national school meal programme has been bolstered through a contribution of US$1 million from the Lions Clubs International Foundation (LCIF), in partnership with World Food Program USA. Media clip in English only.

chunks.h: LCIF and World Food Program USA
chunks.t: Read more School Feeding Initiative Launched in Karamoja October 24, 2024 – A one-million-dollar school feeding initiative is supporting more than 200,000 students across the Karamoja region of Uganda. By improving access to nutritious meals, the program aims to strengthen school attendance, enhance retention and build a healthier future for children and their communities. Media clip in English only. Read more Joint Initiative to Support School Mid-Day Meals in Nepal Launched July 18, 2024 – World Food Program USA and Lions Clubs International Foundation (LCIF), the charitable arm of Lions International, have announced a US$4 million partnership in support of the United Nations World Food Programme’s (WFP) Homegrown School Feeding (HGSF) Programme in four countries, including Nepal. Media clip in English only.

chunks.h: Information for Childhood Cancer Chairperson
chunks.t: Childhood Cancer Chairpersons serve at the district and multiple district levels, and are appointed by the district governor or council chairperson, respectively. Childhood Cancer Chairpersons support Lions and Leos engaged or interested in projects to expand access to life-saving treatment and provide support to the children and families who face childhood cancers. They may collaborate with leadership throughout the organization, including the Global Service Team (GST). Learn Become the topic expert for your district/multiple district by learning about childhood cancers. Become familiar with childhood cancer via the World Health Organization (WHO): Childhood Cancer Key Facts.

chunks.h: Information for Childhood Cancer Chairperson
chunks.t: Explore Lion Portal, LCI/LCIF’s social media sites, and the annual Leo Video Contest to learn more about how Lions and Leos are addressing similar challenges and opportunities in their communities. Discover Bring your knowledge to the local level by exploring how childhood cancer is directly impacting your district/multiple district. Conduct a Community Needs Assessment with a special focus on childhood cancer. Contact your local department of public health, children’s hospital, childhood cancer registry, and other relevant organizations to learn about the needs of local children with cancer and their families. Identify organizations, including Lions and Leos Clubs in your district/multiple district, which are already mobilized, and assess where there are gaps in the services provided.

chunks.h: Information for Childhood Cancer Chairperson
chunks.t: Plan Based upon what you have learned and discovered, submit a plan of action including recommended service goals for childhood cancer to the district governor/council chairperson for approval. In this process, you may wish to:Meet with organizations already working on childhood cancer to discuss how you might support, expand upon, or compliment their ongoing work. Discuss your service plan with the GST Coordinator and other leaders, including other programmatic chairpersons, for their feedback. It is possible they are already implementing a project that would benefit from inclusion of a childhood cancer-related service element. Act Inspiring Lion and Leo clubs in your district/multiple district to serve and report their service to Lion Portal will be critical to the success of your plan.

chunks.h: Information for Childhood Cancer Chairperson
chunks.t: Guide clubs in your district/multiple district through the “Learn, Discover, Act” journey as it pertains to childhood cancer. Build awareness of the need, the goals and the service plan by offering a childhood cancer-focused seminar during district/multiple district convention, and hands-on service activity on February 15, International Childhood Cancer Day. Promote funding opportunities offered through LCI and LCIF that might support club/district childhood cancer projects. Formalize partnerships with other organizations to enhance local impact. Organize a district/multiple district donation to LCIF for childhood cancer to increase global impact. Establish and maintain open communication with the district governor, council chairperson and Global Service Team (GST) leaders.

chunks.h: Information for Childhood Cancer Chairperson
chunks.t: Celebrate Encourage clubs to thoroughly report their childhood cancer projects using Lion Portal. Keep the district governor/council chairperson and GST Coordinator informed. Discuss and evaluate progress of the action plan and goals. Share news about childhood cancer projects with the Public Relations Chairperson. Celebrate progress and success by recognizing all participating clubs. Contact Us Lions Clubs International Phone: 630-571-5466

chunks.h: Leo/Leo-Lion Cabinet and Council Liaison
chunks.t: Leo and Leo-Lion District cabinet and multiple district council liaisons The district cabinet and multiple district council liaison positions appointed to Leos and Leo-Lions are important advisory roles that help facilitate communication between Leos and Lions within districts and multiple districts, in turn improving the Leo Club Program and opportunities for Young Lions. Helpful resources The following resources can help support Leo and Leo-Lion cabinet or council liaisons through their journey in these respective roles. Consider bookmarking this page to keep these links handy for convenient reference when needed. Remember to register and log into the Lion Portal to access additional online leadership training courses and other helpful digital tools.
